draft.title: Independent, dependent and controlled variables
card: A variable is anything in an investigation that can change. In a fair test, you change only one variable and keep the rest the same.
Independent
the variable you change on purpose, such as the amount of light a plant gets.
Dependent
the variable you measure to see what happened, such as the height of the plant. Its result depends on the change you made.
Controlled
every other variable, which you keep the same, such as the soil, water and pot size. Then any change in the dependent variable can be put down to the independent variable.
draft.remember: Change one, measure one, keep the rest the same.

a.q: Sam tests how the temperature of water affects how fast sugar dissolves. Which is the dependent variable?
opts: The time the sugar takes to dissolve
a.why: The time to dissolve is what Sam measures, and it depends on the change he makes. The temperature is the tempting wrong answer, because it is the variable he changes, so it is the independent variable.
a.clue: Which one is measured to see the result?

b.q: Priya tests how the slope of a ramp affects how far a toy car rolls. She uses a different car on each ramp. Why is this not a fair test?
opts: The type of car is not kept the same
The slope of the ramp was changed
b.why: Using a different car changes a second variable, so Priya cannot tell whether slope or car caused the difference. Changing the slope is correct, because it is the independent variable.
b.clue: Which variable should have been kept the same?

a.best: The time the sugar takes to dissolve

b.best: The type of car is not kept the same

problems.detail: The why says "Changing the slope is correct". A student who picked the wrong option "The slope of the ramp was changed" could read this as saying their answer was right. It should say something like "Changing the slope is not the problem, because it is the independent variable."

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct. One option is right in each question. The why for (b) is worded so that "Changing the slope is correct" could make students think the slope option was the right answer.
